items.title: Derrick Gardner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 9, 2013
items.q: I knew some of the music, but the Basie band has their own way of playing what is written on the page... for instance there’s a piece in there, an Ernie Wilkins’ piece called “Right On Right On.”

ctx.x: Ernie Wilkins, yeah, oh man, Ernie Wilkins. So those were the people who formed the Basie sound. And when they brought in an arrangement to the band, oh it was even worse then. Because that’s when Basie was alive it was in its heyday. And that’s when Basie would kind of carve up the arrangement and say “that section right there, on the bridge © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-

there, the horns you all lay out, I’m gonna take that.” Oh big old — you know it could be like this thick orchestrated thing, you know, all this counterpoint, all this other stuff, and Basie says “cut it out, I’m gonna take that.” What?
